newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-HINGIS BATTLES INTO TOSHIBA CLASSIC SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS BATTLES INTO TOSHIBA CLASSIC SEMIFINALS.

text.p: World number one
Martina Hingis fought off a determined challenge from seventh
seed Conchita Martinez Friday to advance to the semifinals of
the Toshiba Tennis Classic.
Just five days after blowing out the Spaniard in a final
at Palo Alto to claim her eighth title of the year, Hingis
needed eight match points to close out a 6-4 6-4 quarter-final
victory.
"I think it was a very good match. You don't know what's
going to happen 'til the end," said Hingis after needing one
hour and 42 minutes to run her 1997 record to 52-1.
"She hit some really good returns and she was fighting
'til the end. It was one of the hardest matches for me and I'm
really happy what I did out there today," added Hingis, who
awaits the survivor of an all French contest between sixth
seed Mary Pierce and Sandrine Testud.
Last Sunday, the 16-year-old Swiss sensation drubbed a
weary Martinez 6-2 6-0 in 53 minutes to win the Bank of West
title. The Spaniard was ready to make a better showing Friday.
"It was a great match. I was very rested today," said
Martinez, the 1994 Wimbledon winner. "I had my chances for
sure. It's good I gave her a very good match. Hopefully next
time I can beat her."
Hingis, this year's Wimbledon winner, had her hands full
with the 10th-ranked Spaniard's array of topspin groundstrokes
in Friday's much more entertaining match.
"Conchita was much stronger this time," noted Hingis, who
managed to convert just four of 16 break opportunities. "She
knew what she had to do against me and she did it pretty
well."
Hingis claimed the opening set with a pair of service
breaks and built a 5-2 advantage in the second before Martinez
took advantage of a mental lapse by the top seed.
The Spaniard successfully fought off three match points in
the ninth game to reach 4-5, leaving a frustrated Hingis
swatting balls into the net in anger.
"She was really hard to finish off," Hingis said. "When
you're leading 6-4, 5-2, you're already thinking it's over.
"You kind of think it's gonna end by itself but it
doesn't."
With Hingis serving for the match at 5-4, Martinez saved
four more match points before finally succumbing when she
slapped a backhand service return into the net on the eighth
match point of the contest.
